items.headline: Singapore to make Marburg, Lassa and Crimean-Congo fevers notifiable from Oct 31
items.summary: From 31 October, doctors and clinical laboratories must report every suspected or confirmed case of Marburg virus, Lassa fever and Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever. The Communicable Diseases Agency says the three viral haemorrhagic fevers have no approved cure, but Singapore's risk level remains low.

items.headline: Singaporean man jailed 19 years and given 24 strokes for abusing six boys
items.summary: A 34-year-old man was sentenced over the sexual abuse of six boys committed between 2010 and 2014, crimes that surfaced only in 2019 when he emailed police to confess. He pleaded guilty to six charges and received 19 years' jail and the maximum 24 strokes of the cane.

items.headline: PM Wong says the government will not cap prices despite cost-of-living strains
items.summary: Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said Singapore will not intervene to cap prices, arguing that controls distort markets, even as he acknowledged households feel the squeeze. He pointed to targeted support rather than blanket subsidies to ease living costs.

items.headline: Singapore leans on quiet diplomacy as haze and gas tensions with Indonesia simmer
items.summary: Singapore's foreign minister made a low-key visit to Jakarta to meet President Prabowo as the neighbours manage friction over cross-border haze and a roughly 8% cut to piped gas. Singapore has summoned firms linked to the fires and plans to amend its Transboundary Haze Pollution Act.

items.headline: Indian court orders takedown of documentary alleging Modi-Adani ties
items.summary: The Calcutta High Court barred the publication and sharing of a documentary by Hotmail co-founder Sabeer Bhatia that accuses Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Gautam Adani of cronyism, until 31 January. Adani Enterprises, which is suing for 500 million rupees in damages, called the film defamatory; the government and the Adani group deny the allegations.

items.headline: Trump says a US-India trade deal is 'pretty close'
items.summary: President Donald Trump said Washington and New Delhi were near an interim trade agreement, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio called the talks 'very, very close' after meeting Indian counterpart S. Jaishankar. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said any deal would protect farmers and other sensitive interests.

items.headline: UK PM Burnham says he wants to discuss a return to EU free movement
items.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he is open to discussing a return to free movement of workers with the EU as part of a wider reset, arguing Brexit had done 'more harm than good'. Reform UK leader Nigel Farage called the remarks a betrayal of Brexit.

items.headline: Burnham weighs single-market and customs-union options ahead of Brussels summit
items.summary: Options for resetting UK-EU ties could include rejoining the single market, the customs union or the bloc itself, with proposals expected around a November summit in Brussels, Bloomberg reported. The government has signalled that parts of the post-Brexit trade deal will be renegotiated.

items.headline: Polls favour Democrats as Trump cancels rallies four days before US midterms
items.summary: With the 3 November US midterms four days away, Democrats led Republicans 51.4% to 43.2% in the RealClearPolling average, with more than 44 million early votes already cast. President Donald Trump cancelled rallies in Kansas and Iowa in favour of telephone events across nearly 20 states.

items.headline: UN commission says Russian strikes on Ukraine's power grid are war crimes
items.summary: A United Nations commission of inquiry concluded that Russia's sustained attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure amount to war crimes, saying they weaponise the cold of winter against civilians. Ukraine says its grid has been struck more than 350 times since September.

items.headline: UAE court jails eight for life over arms supplies to Sudan's army
items.summary: A court in the United Arab Emirates sentenced eight people to life imprisonment for trafficking arms and laundering money to Sudan's armed forces. The case comes amid strained ties between Abu Dhabi and Khartoum, which accuses the UAE of backing the rival Rapid Support Forces, an allegation the UAE denies.

items.headline: OpenAI plans to buy Google's AI chips to diversify beyond Nvidia
items.summary: OpenAI intends to purchase Google's tensor processing units as part of its AI build-out, moving from renting the chips to owning them, Bloomberg reported. Terms are not final and neither company has confirmed the plan, which would deepen ties between the two AI rivals.

items.headline: Nvidia in talks to backstop billions in debt for an Nscale data centre
items.summary: Nvidia is discussing guaranteeing billions of dollars of debt for an Nscale AI data-centre campus in West Virginia that would run on its chips and serve Anthropic's $45 billion compute agreement. The talks are unresolved and terms could still change.

items.headline: Wall Street sell-off deepens as AI-spending fears grip markets
items.summary: US stocks fell for a second day on Friday, with the S&P 500 down about 1.8% and the Nasdaq off roughly 2.9%, as weak results from Amazon and Intel revived doubts about returns on AI spending. Nvidia dropped more than 5% and investors rotated into defensive sectors and government bonds.

items.headline: Intel plunges on weak outlook despite a third-quarter earnings beat
items.summary: Intel shares tumbled sharply after it guided fourth-quarter revenue to $15-16 billion, below the roughly $17 billion expected, citing a prolonged PC slowdown. Adjusted third-quarter earnings of $0.52 a share had beaten estimates, and Intel Foundry revenue rose 58% to $6.7 billion but remained loss-making.

items.headline: Update: Amazon shares slide as record capex overshadows 39% AWS growth
items.summary: Amazon's quarterly revenue of about $202 billion narrowly missed forecasts and free cash flow turned deeply negative as AI spending climbed, pulling shares lower after an initial after-hours pop. Cloud unit AWS was the bright spot, with sales up 39% year on year.

items.headline: Exxon and Chevron beat estimates on strong refining profits
items.summary: ExxonMobil posted adjusted earnings of about $17.5 billion, or $4.23 a share, while Chevron reported roughly $10.4 billion, or $5.28 a share, both topping expectations. Refining margins drove the gains, with Exxon's energy-products unit earning $7.2 billion.

items.headline: 🏎️ Leclerc tops opening practice in Mexico City as rookies take to the track
items.summary: Ferrari's Charles Leclerc led first practice for the Mexico City Grand Prix ahead of Kimi Antonelli, with Mercedes running reserve driver Frederik Vesti in place of George Russell for the mandatory rookie session. The race is on Sunday.

items.headline: 🏎️ Antonelli can clinch the 2026 F1 title in Mexico with a top-nine finish
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli leads the drivers' championship on 365 points from George Russell (242) and Lewis Hamilton (241), and a finish of ninth or better on Sunday would seal his first title regardless of other results. He also holds the tiebreak on race wins.

items.headline: 🎾 Zverev routs Fery to reach the Vienna semi-finals
items.summary: Alexander Zverev beat Britain's Arthur Fery 6-0, 6-2 in under an hour to make his third Vienna semi-final, keeping alive his bid for the year-end world No. 1 ranking. He next faces the winner of Alex de Minaur and Matteo Berrettini.

items.headline: 🏏 South Africa set Australia 288 to win the Cape Town Test
items.summary: Centuries from Ryan Rickelton (101) and Wiaan Mulder (115) carried South Africa to 387 in their second innings, leaving Australia a target of 288 on the final day of the third Test at Newlands. Australia had earlier posted 429, with Josh Inglis making 102.

items.headline: One of the oldest Mars meteorites reveals a wetter early Red Planet
items.summary: A NASA-funded study in Science describes Teghaza 001, a 4.1-billion-year-old Martian meteorite found in the Sahara in 2022 and among the oldest ever identified. Its minerals point to a surprisingly dynamic early water cycle, and researchers matched its chemistry to 13 sites in Mars's southern highlands.

items.headline: The newborn brain purges billions of mutation-riddled neurons
items.summary: Research reported by Nature finds that around the time of birth the developing human brain eliminates large numbers of neurons carrying chromosomal errors. More than a quarter of sampled fetal-brain neurons had gained or lost chromosome segments, hinting at a built-in quality-control system.

items.headline: 'Stupendously large' black holes ruled out as the source of dark matter
items.summary: A study highlighted by Nature concludes that hypothetical black holes more massive than entire galaxies cannot account for dark matter, because such objects would have left a detectable imprint on the cosmic microwave background that is not observed.

items.headline: Why dengue can come back harder in vaccinated people
items.summary: A human challenge trial that exposed 45 volunteers to a weakened dengue strain is revealing why the disease can return more severely even after vaccination, Nature reported. The findings, published in Science Translational Medicine, could guide better next-generation vaccines.

fun_fact.headline: The Eiffel Tower grows about 15 cm taller in summer heat
fun_fact.body: The Eiffel Tower is taller in summer than in winter. Heat makes its wrought-iron lattice expand, so on the hottest days the 330-metre tower can grow by roughly 15 centimetres (about six inches) before contracting as it cools. Specialists put the swing between the coldest and warmest days at about 12 to 15 centimetres.

puzzle.title: Three Suspects
puzzle.body:
A vase is broken by exactly one of three siblings — Ana, Ben, or Cara.

Ana says: 'Ben broke it.'
Ben says: 'I did not break it.'
Cara says: 'I did not break it.'

Exactly one of these three statements is true. Who broke the vase?
puzzle.approach: Test each sibling as the culprit and count how many statements end up true.
puzzle.answer:
Cara broke the vase.

Test each case against 'exactly one true statement':
• If Ana did it: Ana false, Ben true, Cara true → 2 true. No.
• If Ben did it: Ana true, Ben false, Cara true → 2 true. No.
• If Cara did it: Ana false, Ben true, Cara false → exactly 1 true. Correct.
So Cara is the only culprit consistent with the clue.

word_puzzle.title: Spellbound
word_puzzle.body:
Letter Boxed — four sides, three letters each. Build words by hopping from one side to another (never two letters from the same side in a row). Each new word starts with the previous word's last letter, and together the words must use all 12 letters.

Top:    A · I · P
Right:  R · U · N
Bottom: D · M · W
Left:   Z · L · G

Goal: solve it in just two words.
word_puzzle.approach: Chain two words across the four sides; the second word starts with the first word's last letter, and no move may link two letters on the same side.
word_puzzle.answer:
WIZARD → DUMPLING

The two words together use all 12 letters, and WIZARD ends in D so DUMPLING can follow.
WIZARD: W(bottom) → I(top) → Z(left) → A(top) → R(right) → D(bottom).
DUMPLING: D(bottom) → U(right) → M(bottom) → P(top) → L(left) → I(top) → N(right) → G(left).
No two back-to-back letters sit on the same side.
